nodes.name: Supersymmetrization of GESM theories
nodes.statement: The supersymmetrization of the theories introduced in this paper is currently an open problem involving several objects and structures of mathematical interest, such as spinor bundles and Lipschitz structures, Special-K\"ahler and Quaternionic-K\"ahler manifolds or exceptional Lie groups, all interacting in a delicate equilibrium dictated by supersymmetry.
nodes.statement_short: Supersymmetrizing the theories of this paper is open and involves spinor bundles, Lipschitz structures and special holonomy target geometries.

nodes.name: Integrable case: global solutions are classical locally-geometric U-folds
nodes.statement: When the Kaluza-Klein space is integrable, global solutions of the GESM theory correspond to classical locally-geometric U-folds glued from local solutions of the ordinary sigma model coupled to Abelian gauge fields (which may have a non-trivial duality structure) using symmetries of the equations of motion of the latter.
nodes.statement_short: If the Kaluza-Klein space is integrable, GESM solutions are U-folds glued from ordinary-sigma-model solutions via symmetries of the equations of motion.
assumptions: When the Kaluza-Klein space is integrable
conclusions: global solutions of the GESM theory correspond to classical locally-geometric U-folds glued from local solutions of the ordinary sigma model coupled to Abelian gauge fields (which may have a non-trivial duality structure) using symmetries of the equations of motion of the latter.

nodes.name: Non-integrable case: gluing from the modified sigma model
nodes.statement: When the Kaluza-Klein space is not integrable, global solutions of the GESM theory can be glued from local solutions of the modified sigma model coupled to Abelian gauge fields (which may have a non-trivial duality structure).
nodes.statement_short: In the non-integrable case, global GESM solutions glue from local solutions of the modified sigma model coupled to Abelian gauge fields.
assumptions: When the Kaluza-Klein space is not integrable
conclusions: global solutions of the GESM theory can be glued from local solutions of the modified sigma model coupled to Abelian gauge fields (which may have a non-trivial duality structure).

nodes.name: Local (in)distinguishability of GESM from ESM theories
nodes.statement: Together with the results of \cite{GESM}, point A. above implies that GESM theories with integrable Kaluza-Klein space are {\em locally} indistinguishable from usual Einstein-Scalar-Maxwell theories and hence provide admissible global interpretations of the local formulas governing the universal bosonic sector of four-dimensional supergravity. On the other hand, point B. above implies that GESM theories with non-integrable Kaluza-Klein space are {\em locally distinct} from ordinary ESM theories.
nodes.statement_short: Integrable GESM theories are locally indistinguishable from ESM theories; non-integrable ones are locally distinct.
assumptions: GESM theories with integrable Kaluza-Klein space

nodes.name: Blanket smoothness and connectedness assumptions
nodes.statement: All manifolds considered are smooth, connected, Hausdorff and paracompact (hence also second countable) while all fiber bundles considered are smooth. All submersions considered are assumed to be surjective and to have connected fibers.
nodes.statement_short: All manifolds are smooth, connected, Hausdorff, paracompact; all bundles smooth; all submersions surjective with connected fibers.

nodes.name: $\Met_{p,q}(W)$ and $\Met(W)$
nodes.statement: Let $\Met_{p,q}(W)$ denote the set of non-degenerate symmetric pairings of signature $(p,q)$ on a vector bundle $W$ of rank $\rk W=p+q$. Let $\Met(W)\eqdef \sqcup_{p,q\geq 0, p+q=\rk W}\Met_{p,q}(W)$ denote the set of all non-degenerate metrics on $W$. When $W=TM$ is the tangent bundle of a manifold $M$, we set $\Met_{p,q}(M)\eqdef \Met_{p,q}(TM)$ and $\Met(M)\eqdef \Met(TM)$.
nodes.statement_short: Notation for the sets of non-degenerate symmetric pairings of given signature on a vector bundle, and of all non-degenerate metrics.
nodes.genus: the set of non-degenerate symmetric pairings of signature $(p,q)$ on a vector bundle $W$
differentia: of signature $(p,q)$
of rank $\rk W=p+q$

nodes.name: Lorentzian manifold
nodes.statement: By definition, a Lorentzian manifold is a pseudo-Riemannian manifold of ``mostly plus'' signature.
differentia: of ``mostly plus'' signature

nodes.name: $\cP(M)$, the set of paths of $M$
nodes.statement: Given a manifold $M$, let $\cP(M)$ denote the set of paths (piecewise-smooth curves) $\gamma:[0,1]\rightarrow M$.
differentia: $\gamma:[0,1]\rightarrow M$

nodes.name: On the use of the term ``Kaluza-Klein space''
nodes.statement: Throughout the paper, we use the mathematical concept of ``Kaluza-Klein space'', which is well-established in the mathematics and mathematical physics literature (see, for example, \cite{Bourguignon,Hogan,Betounes1,Betounes2,Besse}). Such spaces were initially defined and studied in the context of mathematical foundations of Kaluza-Klein theories, which arise by reducing a higher-dimensional theory of gravity on such a manifold. In the present paper, such spaces are used merely as convenient auxiliary mathematical data which parameterize a GESM theory, despite the historical context in which they were introduced initially. Throughout the paper, no reduction of any putative higher dimensional theory on such spaces is ever suggested or performed.
nodes.statement_short: Kaluza-Klein spaces are used here only as auxiliary data parameterizing a GESM theory; no dimensional reduction is performed.

nodes.name: Dimensions of space-time and total space
nodes.statement: Let $(M,g)$ be a connected four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold. Let $E$ be a connected manifold of dimension $\dim E=n+4$, where $n>0$.
nodes.statement_short: $(M,g)$ is a connected four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold and $E$ is connected of dimension $n+4$ with $n>0$.

nodes.name: surjective submersion
nodes.statement: Recall that a smooth map $\pi:E\rightarrow M$ is called a {\em surjective submersion} if $\pi$ is surjective and the linear map $\dd_e \pi\colon T_e E\rightarrow T_{\pi(e)} M$ is surjective for all $e\in E$.
differentia: $\pi$ is surjective
the linear map $\dd_e \pi\colon T_e E\rightarrow T_{\pi(e)} M$ is surjective for all $e\in E$

nodes.name: vertical distribution of $\pi$
nodes.statement: The {\em vertical distribution} of $\pi$ is the rank $n$ distribution $V\eqdef \ker (\dd \pi)\subset T E$ defined on $E$, which is Frobenius integrable and integrates to the foliation whose leaves are the fibers of $\pi$.
nodes.genus: the rank $n$ distribution $V\eqdef \ker (\dd \pi)\subset T E$ defined on $E$
differentia: Frobenius integrable
integrates to the foliation whose leaves are the fibers of $\pi$

nodes.name: $\pi$-positive metric and horizontal distribution
nodes.statement: A Lorentzian metric $h$ on $E$ is called {\em $\pi$-positive} if its restriction to each fiber of $\pi$ is positive-definite. In this case, the $h$-orthogonal complement $H:=H(h)$ of $V$ inside $TE$ is a distribution of rank four called the {\em horizontal distribution} of $\pi$ determined by $h$.
nodes.statement_short: A Lorentzian metric on $E$ is $\pi$-positive when positive-definite on fibers; its $h$-orthogonal complement of $V$ is the horizontal distribution.
differentia: its restriction to each fiber of $\pi$ is positive-definite

nodes.name: vertical and horizontal metrics induced by $h$
nodes.statement: Let $h_V$ and $h_H$ denote the metrics induced by $h$ on $V$ and $H$, which we call the {\em vertical} and {\em horizontal} metrics induced by $h$.
nodes.genus: the metrics induced by $h$ on $V$ and $H$

nodes.name: $(\dd\pi)_H$ is a based isomorphism onto $(TM)^\pi$
nodes.statement: For any $e\in E$, the map $\dd_e \pi$ restricts to a linear bijection from $H_e$ to $T_{\pi(e)}M$. Hence the restriction $\dd\pi|_H$ of $\dd \pi$ to $H$ induces a based isomorphism of vector bundles $(\dd\pi)_H\colon H\stackrel{\sim}{\rightarrow} (TM)^\pi$.
nodes.statement_short: $\dd_e\pi$ restricts to a linear bijection $H_e\to T_{\pi(e)}M$, giving a bundle isomorphism $(\dd\pi)_H\colon H\to (TM)^\pi$.
assumptions: For any $e\in E$
conclusions: the map $\dd_e \pi$ restricts to a linear bijection from $H_e$ to $T_{\pi(e)}M$
the restriction $\dd\pi|_H$ of $\dd \pi$ to $H$ induces a based isomorphism of vector bundles $(\dd\pi)_H\colon H\stackrel{\sim}{\rightarrow} (TM)^\pi$

nodes.name: Lorentzian submersion
nodes.statement: Let $h$ be a $\pi$-positive Lorentzian metric on $E$. The surjective submersion $\pi:E\rightarrow M$ is called a {\em Lorentzian submersion} from $(E,h)$ to $(M,g)$ if the bundle isomorphism $(\dd\pi)_H$ is an isometry from $(H,h_H)$ to $((TM)^\pi,g^\pi)$.
nodes.statement_short: A surjective submersion is a Lorentzian submersion when $(\dd\pi)_H$ is an isometry from $(H,h_H)$ to $((TM)^\pi,g^\pi)$.
differentia: the bundle isomorphism $(\dd\pi)_H$ is an isometry from $(H,h_H)$ to $((TM)^\pi,g^\pi)$

nodes.name: Signature of $(H,h_H)$ and $(V,h_V)$ for a Lorentzian submersion
nodes.statement: When $\pi$ is a Lorentzian submersion from $(E,h)$ to $(M,g)$, the pair $(H,h_H)$ is a pseudo-Euclidean distribution of signature $(3,1)$ defined on $E$ while $(V,h_V)$ is a Euclidean distribution. In particular, $\pi$ is a surjective pseudo-Riemannian submersion in the sense of \cite{ONeillBook}.
nodes.statement_short: For a Lorentzian submersion, $(H,h_H)$ has signature $(3,1)$ and $(V,h_V)$ is Euclidean, so $\pi$ is a pseudo-Riemannian submersion.
assumptions: When $\pi$ is a Lorentzian submersion from $(E,h)$ to $(M,g)$
conclusions: the pair $(H,h_H)$ is a pseudo-Euclidean distribution of signature $(3,1)$ defined on $E$ while $(V,h_V)$ is a Euclidean distribution
$\pi$ is a surjective pseudo-Riemannian submersion in the sense of \cite{ONeillBook}

nodes.name: Kaluza-Klein metric
nodes.statement: A {\em Kaluza-Klein metric} for the surjective submersion $\pi:E\rightarrow M$ relative to the Lorentzian metric $g\in \Met_{3,1}(M)$ is a $\pi$-positive Lorentzian metric $h$ on $E$ which makes $\pi$ into a Lorentzian submersion from $(E,h)$ to $(M,g)$.
differentia: which makes $\pi$ into a Lorentzian submersion from $(E,h)$ to $(M,g)$

nodes.name: horizontal lift of vector fields and the $H\oplus V$ decomposition
nodes.statement: Any horizontal distribution $H$ defines a horizontal lift of vector fields, which takes $Q\in \cX(M)$ into the unique horizontal vector field $\bar{Q}\in \Gamma(E,H)$ satisfying $\dd\pi(\bar{Q}) = Q$. Moreover, any vector field $X\in \cX(E)$ decomposes uniquely as $X=X_H\oplus X_V$, where $X_H\in \Gamma(E,H)$ and $X_V\in \Gamma(E,V)$.
nodes.statement_short: Each horizontal distribution lifts $Q\in\cX(M)$ to the unique horizontal $\bar Q$ with $\dd\pi(\bar Q)=Q$, and splits every $X\in\cX(E)$ as $X_H\oplus X_V$.

nodes.name: curvature $\cF$ of a horizontal distribution
nodes.statement: The {\em curvature} $\cF\in \Omega^2(E,V)$ of $H$ is defined as \cite{Michor}: \be \cF(X,Y)\eqdef [X_H,Y_H]_V\, , \quad \forall X,Y\in \cX(E)\, . \ee
differentia: \cF(X,Y)\eqdef [X_H,Y_H]_V\, , \quad \forall X,Y\in \cX(E)

nodes.name: Restriction $\cF_H$ of the curvature to $H$
nodes.statement: Its restriction to $H$ gives a section $\cF_H\in \Gamma(E,\wedge^2H^\ast\otimes V)$ which satisfies: \be \cF_H(X,Y)=\cF(X,Y)=[X,Y]_V\, , \quad \forall X,Y\in \Gamma(E,H) \ee
nodes.statement_short: On horizontal vector fields the curvature is just the vertical part of the Lie bracket.

nodes.name: Relation between $\cF_H$ and O'Neill's second fundamental tensor $A$
nodes.statement: and hence coincides up to a constant factor with the restriction to $H$ of O'Neill's second fundamental tensor $A$ \cite{ONeill} of the pseudo-Riemannian submersion $\pi$: \be A_XY=-A_YX=\frac{1}{2}\cF_H(X,Y)\, , \quad \forall X,Y\in \Gamma(E,H)~~. \ee
nodes.statement_short: $\cF_H$ agrees up to the factor $2$ with O'Neill's tensor $A$ of the pseudo-Riemannian submersion.

nodes.name: O'Neill's tensor as the obstruction to integrability of $H$
nodes.statement: A basic property of O'Neill's tensor is that it vanishes if and only if $\cF_H$ does. Hence either of $A$ or $\cF_H$ describe the obstruction to Frobenius integrability of $H$.
nodes.statement_short: $A$ vanishes iff $\cF_H$ does, so either tensor measures the failure of Frobenius integrability of $H$.
assumptions: A basic property of O'Neill's tensor
conclusions: it vanishes if and only if $\cF_H$ does
either of $A$ or $\cF_H$ describe the obstruction to Frobenius integrability of $H$

nodes.name: complete horizontal distribution
nodes.statement: The distribution $H$ is called {\em complete} if the flow $T$ defined by horizontal lifts of vector fields is globally-defined, which amounts to the condition that {\em any} curve in $M$ lifts to a horizontal curve in $E$ through any point lying in the fiber above its source.
differentia: the flow $T$ defined by horizontal lifts of vector fields is globally-defined
{\em any} curve in $M$ lifts to a horizontal curve in $E$ through any point lying in the fiber above its source

nodes.name: Ehresmann's fiber bundle theorem
nodes.statement: When $H$ is complete, it follows from a result of \cite{Ehresmann} that $\pi$ is a fiber bundle, though its structure group need not be a finite-dimensional Lie group.
nodes.statement_short: A complete horizontal distribution makes $\pi$ a fiber bundle, with possibly infinite-dimensional structure group.
assumptions: When $H$ is complete
conclusions: $\pi$ is a fiber bundle, though its structure group need not be a finite-dimensional Lie group

nodes.name: Ehresmann connection and Ehresmann transport
nodes.statement: In this case, $H$ is an Ehresmann connection for $\pi$ and $T$ is called its Ehresmann transport.

nodes.name: Reckziegel's fiber bundle theorem
nodes.statement: Reference \cite{Reckziegel} shows that a sufficient condition for $H$ to be complete and for the structure group to be a finite-dimensional Lie group is that the fibers of $\pi$ be geodesically complete and totally geodesic connected submanifolds of $(E,h)$. In this case the Ehresmann transport $T$ is isometric, which means that $T_\gamma$ is an isometry from $E_{\gamma(0)}$ to $E_{\gamma(1)}$ for any path $\gamma\in \cP(M)$. Hence the structure group is isomorphic to the Riemannian isometry group of the fiber of $\pi$ over any given point in $M$.
nodes.statement_short: Geodesically complete, totally geodesic connected fibers force $H$ to be complete with finite-dimensional structure group and isometric Ehresmann transport.
assumptions: the fibers of $\pi$ be geodesically complete and totally geodesic connected submanifolds of $(E,h)$
conclusions: a sufficient condition for $H$ to be complete and for the structure group to be a finite-dimensional Lie group
the Ehresmann transport $T$ is isometric, which means that $T_\gamma$ is an isometry from $E_{\gamma(0)}$ to $E_{\gamma(1)}$ for any path $\gamma\in \cP(M)$
the structure group is isomorphic to the Riemannian isometry group of the fiber of $\pi$ over any given point in $M$

nodes.name: Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein space
nodes.statement: A {\em Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein space} over $(M,g)$ is a Lorentzian submersion $\pi:(E,h)\rightarrow (M,g)$ such that $(E,h)$ is connected and such that the fibers of $\pi$ are geodesically complete and totally geodesic connected submanifolds of $(E,h)$. The Kaluza-Klein space is called {\em integrable} if the horizontal distribution $H(h)\subset TE$ defined by $h$ is Frobenius integrable.
nodes.statement_short: A Lorentzian submersion with connected total space whose fibers are geodesically complete, totally geodesic connected submanifolds; integrable when $H(h)$ is Frobenius integrable.
differentia: $(E,h)$ is connected
the fibers of $\pi$ are geodesically complete and totally geodesic connected submanifolds of $(E,h)$

nodes.name: The Kaluza-Klein metric is determined by $g$, $\cG$ and $H$
nodes.statement: Consider a Lorentzian Kaluza-Klein space $\pi:(E,h)\rightarrow (M,g)$ with horizontal distribution $H:=H(h)$, whose Ehresmann transport we denote by $T:=T(h)$. Let $m_0$ be fixed point of $M$ and let $\cM\eqdef E_{m_0}=\pi^{-1}(\{m_0\})$ and $\cG\eqdef h|_{E_{m_0}}$. As mentioned above, the results of \cite{Reckziegel} imply that $H$ is a complete Ehresmann connection, that $\pi$ is a fiber bundle and that the transport $T$ is isometric. Hence the restriction $h_m\eqdef h|_{E_m}$ of $h$ to the fibers of $E$ is uniquely determined by $\cG$ and by $T$. Therefore, the metric $h$ of a Kaluza-Klein space is uniquely determined by $g$, $\cG$ and $H$.
nodes.statement_short: Isometry of the Ehresmann transport forces $h$ to be fixed by the base metric, the fiber metric and the horizontal distribution.

nodes.name: Bijection between Ehresmann connections and Kaluza-Klein metrics
nodes.statement: When $g$ and $\cG$ are fixed, we thus have a bijection between Ehresmann connections $H$ for $\pi$ and Lorentzian metrics $h$ on $E$ such that $\pi:(E,h)\rightarrow (M,g)$ is a Kaluza-Klein space and such that $h_{m_0}=\cG$.
nodes.statement_short: With $g$ and $\cG$ fixed, Ehresmann connections $H$ correspond bijectively to Kaluza-Klein metrics $h$ with $h_{m_0}=\cG$.

nodes.name: Ehresmann holonomy group at $m_0$
nodes.statement: Let: \be G\eqdef \{T_\gamma\, , \,\, |\,\, \gamma\in \cP(M)\, , \quad \gamma(0)=\gamma(1)=m_0\}\subseteq \Iso(\cM,\cG) \ee be the Ehresmann holonomy group at $m_0$.

nodes.name: holonomy bundle $\Pi$ of $H$ relative to $m_0$
nodes.statement: For any $m\in M$, consider the set: \be \Pi_m \eqdef \{T_\gamma\,\, |\,\, \gamma\in \cP(M): \gamma(0)=m_0\,\, \&\,\, \gamma(1)=m\}\, , \ee and let $\Pi\eqdef \sqcup_{m\in M}\Pi_m$ be endowed with the obvious projection to $M$. Then $\Pi$ is a principal $G$-bundle (known as the {\em holonomy bundle} of $H$ relative to $m_0$) under the obvious right action of $G$. Moreover, the Ehresmann connection $H$ induces a principal connection $\theta$ on $\Pi$.
nodes.statement_short: The disjoint union of the transport sets $\Pi_m$ is a principal $G$-bundle carrying a principal connection $\theta$ induced by $H$.

nodes.name: Quasi-inverse functors between Kaluza-Klein spaces and principal bundles
nodes.statement: Conversely, let $\rho$ be the isometric action of $G$ on $\cM$ given by the inclusion $G\subseteq \Iso(\cM,\cG)$. Then the associated bundle construction associates to a principal bundle $\Pi$ with principal connection $\theta$ the fiber bundle $E_\Pi\eqdef \Pi\times_\rho \cM$ with induced Ehresmann connection $H_\theta$. The two correspondences described above give mutually quasi-inverse functors between the groupoid of Kaluza-Klein spaces over $(M,g)$ which have typical fiber $(\cM,\cG)$ and are endowed with a horizontal distribution $H$ with holonomy $G\subseteq \Iso(\cM,\cG)$ and the groupoid of principal $G$-bundles $\Pi$ defined over $M$ and endowed with a principal connection $\theta$ together with an embedding $G\subseteq \Iso(\cM,\cG)$ up to conjugation.
nodes.statement_short: The holonomy-bundle and associated-bundle constructions are mutually quasi-inverse functors between the two groupoids.

nodes.name: Classification of Kaluza-Klein spaces by principal bundles with connection
nodes.statement: Let $g$ be a fixed Lorentzian metric on $M$. Then isomorphism classes of Kaluza-Klein spaces over $(M,g)$ with typical fiber $(\cM,\cG)$ and horizontal distribution $H$ having Ehresmann holonomy contained in $\Iso(\cM,\cG)$ are in bijection with isomorphism classes of principal $G$-bundles $\Pi$ defined over $M$ and endowed with a principal connection $\theta$ whose holonomy is embedded in $\Iso(\cM,\cG)$. Moreover, $H$ is integrable if and only if $\theta$ is flat.
nodes.statement_short: Isomorphism classes of Kaluza-Klein spaces with fixed typical fiber correspond to principal $G$-bundles with connection; integrability corresponds to flatness of $\theta$.
assumptions: Let $g$ be a fixed Lorentzian metric on $M$
conclusions: isomorphism classes of Kaluza-Klein spaces over $(M,g)$ with typical fiber $(\cM,\cG)$ and horizontal distribution $H$ having Ehresmann holonomy contained in $\Iso(\cM,\cG)$ are in bijection with isomorphism classes of principal $G$-bundles $\Pi$ defined over $M$ and endowed with a principal connection $\theta$ whose holonomy is embedded in $\Iso(\cM,\cG)$
$H$ is integrable if and only if $\theta$ is flat

nodes.name: The trivial bundle $\pi^0:M\times\cM\rightarrow M$ and its vertical distribution
nodes.statement: Let $(\cM,\cG)$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $E^{0} \eqdef M\times\cM$ and let $\pi^0:M\times \cM\rightarrow M$ and $p^0:M\times\cM\rightarrow \cM$ denote the canonical projections. Notice that $\pi^0$ is the trivial fiber bundle over $M$ with fiber $\cM$. Let $V^0=(T\cM)^{p^0}$ denote the vertical distribution of $\pi^0$, which is endowed with the pull-back metric $\cG^{p^0}$.

nodes.name: topologically trivial Kaluza-Klein space
nodes.statement: A {\em topologically trivial Kaluza-Klein space} over $(M,g)$ with fiber $(\cM,\cG)$ is a Kaluza-Klein space of the form $\pi^0:(E^0,h^{0})\rightarrow (M,g)$, whose vertical metric is the pull-back metric $h_{V^0}\eqdef \cG^{p^0}$.
nodes.genus: a Kaluza-Klein space of the form $\pi^0:(E^0,h^{0})\rightarrow (M,g)$
differentia: whose vertical metric is the pull-back metric $h_{V^0}\eqdef \cG^{p^0}$

nodes.name: The metric of a topologically trivial Kaluza-Klein space is determined by $g$, $\cG$, $H$
nodes.statement: The metric $h^{0}=h(g,\cG,H)$ of such a space is uniquely determined by $g$, $\cG$ and by the horizontal distribution $H$, whose parallel transport $T$ must preserve $\cG^{p^0}$.

nodes.name: Fiberwise form ${\hat T}_\gamma$ of the Ehresmann transport
nodes.statement: For any $\gamma\in \cP(M)$ and all $p\in \cM$, we define: \ben T_\gamma(\gamma(0),p)=(\gamma(1),{\hat T}_\gamma(p))~~, \een where ${\hat T}_\gamma\in \Iso(\cM,\cG)$ satisfy ${\hat T}_{\gamma_1\gamma_2}={\hat T}_{\gamma_1}\circ {\hat T}_{\gamma_2}$.
nodes.statement_short: On a trivial bundle the transport is $T_\gamma(\gamma(0),p)=(\gamma(1),\hat T_\gamma(p))$ with $\hat T$ a homomorphism into $\Iso(\cM,\cG)$.

nodes.name: product Kaluza-Klein space
nodes.statement: The {\em product Kaluza-Klein space} over $(M,g)$ with fiber $(\cM,\cG)$ is the topologically trivial Kaluza-Klein space $\pi^0:(E^0,h^0_{\triv})\rightarrow (M,g)$ with fiber $(\cM,\cG)$ whose horizontal distribution is the trivial integrable Ehresmann connection $H^0_{\triv} \eqdef (T M)^{\pi^0}$, with induced horizontal metric $h^0_{\triv}$.
nodes.genus: the topologically trivial Kaluza-Klein space $\pi^0:(E^0,h^0_{\triv})\rightarrow (M,g)$ with fiber $(\cM,\cG)$
differentia: whose horizontal distribution is the trivial integrable Ehresmann connection $H^0_{\triv} \eqdef (T M)^{\pi^0}$

nodes.name: The trivial Ehresmann connection yields the product metric
nodes.statement: For any $p\in \cM$, the horizontal lift through $(\gamma(0),p)\in E^0_{\gamma(0)}$ of any path $\gamma\in \cP(M)$ defined by the trivial Ehresmann connection $H^0$ is the path given by $\bgamma_{p, \triv}(s)=(\gamma(s),p)$ for all $s\in [0,1]$. Hence the Ehresmann transport $T^0_\gamma$ defined by $H^0$ is given by ${\hat T}^0_{\gamma}=\id_{\cM}$. This implies that the Kaluza-Klein metric $h^0_{\triv}=h_{g, \cG, H^0_\triv}$ equals the product metric $g\times \cG$.
nodes.statement_short: Horizontal lifts for $H^0$ are constant in the fiber, $\hat T^0_\gamma=\id_\cM$, so $h^0_{\triv}=g\times\cG$.

nodes.name: Classification of flat principal bundles by their holonomy morphism
nodes.statement: It is well-known that flat principal $G$-bundles are classified up to isomorphism by their holonomy morphism $\Hol_{P,\theta}:\pi_1(M)\rightarrow G$, considered up to the conjugation action of $G$.
nodes.statement_short: Flat principal $G$-bundles are classified up to isomorphism by $\Hol_{P,\theta}:\pi_1(M)\to G$ modulo conjugation.
assumptions: flat principal $G$-bundles
conclusions: are classified up to isomorphism by their holonomy morphism $\Hol_{P,\theta}:\pi_1(M)\rightarrow G$, considered up to the conjugation action of $G$

nodes.name: Integrable Kaluza-Klein spaces are classified by a character variety
nodes.statement: Hence the set of isomorphism classes of integrable Kaluza-Klein spaces over $(M,g)$ with fiber $(\cM,\cG)$ and Ehresmann holonomy contained in $\Iso(\cM,\cG)$ is in bijection with the character variety: \begin{equation*} \cM_{\Iso(\cM,\cG)}(M)\eqdef \Hom(\pi_1(M),\Iso(\cM,\cG))/\Iso(\cM,\cG)\, . \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Isomorphism classes of integrable Kaluza-Klein spaces correspond to points of $\Hom(\pi_1(M),\Iso(\cM,\cG))/\Iso(\cM,\cG)$.
assumptions: integrable Kaluza-Klein spaces over $(M,g)$ with fiber $(\cM,\cG)$ and Ehresmann holonomy contained in $\Iso(\cM,\cG)$
conclusions: is in bijection with the character variety: \begin{equation*} \cM_{\Iso(\cM,\cG)}(M)\eqdef \Hom(\pi_1(M),\Iso(\cM,\cG))/\Iso(\cM,\cG)\, . \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Simply-connected space-time forces a product Kaluza-Klein space
nodes.statement: When the space-time $M$ is simply-connected, any integrable Kaluza-Klein space over $(M,g)$ is isomorphic with a product space (see below). In that case, we necessarily have $G=1$ (the trivial group) and $H$ is gauge-equivalent with the trivial Ehresmann connection.
nodes.statement_short: If $M$ is simply connected, every integrable Kaluza-Klein space is a product and $G$ is trivial.
assumptions: When the space-time $M$ is simply-connected
conclusions: any integrable Kaluza-Klein space over $(M,g)$ is isomorphic with a product space
we necessarily have $G=1$ (the trivial group) and $H$ is gauge-equivalent with the trivial Ehresmann connection

nodes.name: vertical scalar potential
nodes.statement: A \emph{vertical scalar potential} for $\pi$ is a smooth $T$-invariant real-valued function $\bPhi \in \cC^\infty(E,\R)$ defined on the total space $E$ of $\pi$.
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles
differentia: $T$-invariant
defined on the total space $E$ of $\pi$

nodes.name: $T$-invariance of $\bPhi$ and its infinitesimal form
nodes.statement: The $T$-invariance of $\bPhi$ means that the restrictions $\Phi_m\eqdef \bPhi|_{E_m}\in \cC^\infty(E_m,\R)$ to the fibers of $E$ satisfy: \be \Phi_{\gamma(1)}\circ T_\gamma=\Phi_{\gamma(0)}\, ,\quad \forall\,\, \gamma\in \cP(M)~~, \ee a condition which is equivalent with the requirement that $\bPhi$ is annihilated by any horizontal vector field defined on $E$: \ben X(\bPhi)=0\, , \quad \forall\, X\in \Gamma(E,H)\, . \een
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles
nodes.statement_short: $T$-invariance of $\bPhi$ is equivalent to annihilation by all horizontal vector fields, $X(\bPhi)=0$.

nodes.name: Fiber restrictions of $\bPhi$ are recovered from one fiber and preserved by holonomy
nodes.statement: This implies that all fiber restrictions $\Phi_m$ ($m\in M$) can be recovered from $\Phi_{m_0}$, where $m_0$ is any fixed point of $M$. In particular, the isomorphism type of the scalar structure\footnote{As defined in reference \cite{GESM}.} $(E_m,h_m,\Phi_m)$ is independent of $m$. The holonomy group $G_{m}\subset \Iso(E_{m},h_{m})$ of $\pi$ at any point $m\in M$ preserves $\Phi_{m}$: \be G_m \subset \Iso(E_m, h_m, \Phi_m)\eqdef \{\varphi\in \Iso(E_m,h_m)|\Phi_m\circ \varphi=\Phi_m\}~~. \ee
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles
nodes.statement_short: All $\Phi_m$ follow from $\Phi_{m_0}$, the scalar structure type is $m$-independent, and $G_m$ preserves $\Phi_m$.

nodes.name: The gradient of a vertical scalar potential is vertical
nodes.statement: Relation \eqref{Vvert} amounts to $\dd \bPhi (X)=0$ for all $X\in\Gamma(X,H)$, i.e. $\dd \bPhi \circ P_H=0$. Since $P_V+P_H=\id_{TE}$, this gives $\dd \bPhi=\dd \bPhi \circ P_V$, which shows that $\dd \bPhi$ can be viewed as an element of $\Gamma(E,V^\ast)$. Since $H$ and $V$ are $h$-orthogonal, this implies that the gradient of $\bPhi$ is a vertical vector field: \be \grad_h \bPhi\in \Gamma(E,V)~~. \ee
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles
nodes.statement_short: Since $\dd\bPhi\circ P_H=0$ and $H\perp_h V$, one gets $\grad_h\bPhi\in\Gamma(E,V)$.

nodes.name: scalar bundle
nodes.statement: A {\em scalar bundle} over $(M,g)$ is a pair $(\pi:(E,h)\rightarrow (M,g),\bPhi)$, where $\pi$ is a Kaluza-Klein space and $\bPhi$ is a vertical scalar potential for $\pi$. The scalar bundle is called {\em integrable} if the Kaluza-Klein space $\pi$ is integrable.
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles
differentia: $\pi$ is a Kaluza-Klein space
$\bPhi$ is a vertical scalar potential for $\pi$

nodes.name: type of a scalar bundle
nodes.statement: The isomorphism type of the scalar structures $(E_m,h_m,\Phi_m)$ (which, as explained above, does not depend on the point $m\in M$) is called the {\em type} of the scalar bundle and will be generally denoted by $(\cM,\cG,\Phi)$.
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles
nodes.genus: The isomorphism type of the scalar structures $(E_m,h_m,\Phi_m)$

nodes.name: Classification of integrable scalar bundles
nodes.statement: Integrable scalar bundles defined over $(M,g)$ and having type $(\cM,\cG,\Phi)$ are classified up to isomorphism by the points of the character variety: \be \cM_{\Iso(\cM,\cG,\Phi)}(M)\eqdef \Hom(\pi_1(M),\Iso(\cM,\cG,\Phi))/\Iso(\cM,\cG,\Phi)~~. \ee
nodes.section: 2.3 Vertical scalar potentials and scalar bundles
nodes.statement_short: Integrable scalar bundles of type $(\cM,\cG,\Phi)$ are classified by the character variety of $\pi_1(M)$ in $\Iso(\cM,\cG,\Phi)$.
assumptions: Integrable scalar bundles defined over $(M,g)$ and having type $(\cM,\cG,\Phi)$
conclusions: are classified up to isomorphism by the points of the character variety: \be \cM_{\Iso(\cM,\cG,\Phi)}(M)\eqdef \Hom(\pi_1(M),\Iso(\cM,\cG,\Phi))/\Iso(\cM,\cG,\Phi)~~. \ee

nodes.name: geodesically convex open subset
nodes.statement: Recall that an open subset $U$ of a pseudo-Riemannian manifold is called {\em geodesically convex} \cite{ONeillBook} if it is a normal neighborhood for each of its points. If $U$ is convex, then for any two points $p,q\in U$ there exists a unique geodesic segment which is contained in $U$ and which connects $p$ and $q$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.genus: an open subset $U$ of a pseudo-Riemannian manifold
differentia: it is a normal neighborhood for each of its points

nodes.name: Existence of a basis of geodesically convex neighborhoods
nodes.statement: Any point of a pseudo-Riemannian manifold has a basis of geodesically convex neighborhoods (see \cite[p. 129]{ONeillBook}).
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
assumptions: Any point of a pseudo-Riemannian manifold
conclusions: has a basis of geodesically convex neighborhoods

nodes.name: convex cover
nodes.statement: A {\em convex cover} of a pseudo-Riemannian manifold is an cover by open and geodesically convex sets which has the property that any nontrivial intersection of two of its elements is geodesically convex.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.genus: an cover by open and geodesically convex sets
differentia: any nontrivial intersection of two of its elements is geodesically convex

nodes.name: Existence of convex covers refining a given cover
nodes.statement: Given any open cover $\mathfrak{V}$ of a pseudo-Riemannian manifold, there exists a convex cover $\mathfrak{U}$ such that any element of $\mathfrak{U}$ is contained in some element of $\mathfrak{V}$ \cite[Lemma 5.10]{ONeillBook}. In particular, any pseudo-Riemannian manifold admits convex covers.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.statement_short: Every open cover of a pseudo-Riemannian manifold is refined by a convex cover; in particular convex covers exist.
assumptions: Given any open cover $\mathfrak{V}$ of a pseudo-Riemannian manifold
conclusions: there exists a convex cover $\mathfrak{U}$ such that any element of $\mathfrak{U}$ is contained in some element of $\mathfrak{V}$
any pseudo-Riemannian manifold admits convex covers

nodes.name: special trivializing atlas of a Kaluza-Klein space
nodes.statement: Let $\pi:(E,h)\rightarrow (M,g)$ be a Kaluza-Klein space. Let $m_0 \in M$ be a fixed point and set $\cM\eqdef E_{m_0}$ and $\cG\eqdef h_{m_0}$. Let $\mathfrak{U}=\left( U_\alpha\right)_{\alpha \in I}$ be a convex cover for $(M,g)$, where the indexing set is chosen such that $0\not \in I$. Fix points $m_{\alpha}\in U_\alpha$ and paths $\lambda^{\alpha}\in \cP(M)$ such that $\lambda^{\alpha}(0)=m_{\alpha}$ and $\lambda^{\alpha}(1)=m_0$. For any $m\in U_\alpha$, let $\gamma_m^{\alpha}:[0,1]\rightarrow U_\alpha$ be the unique smooth geodesic contained in $U_\alpha$ such that $\gamma_m^{\alpha}(0)=m$ and $\gamma_m^{\alpha}(1)=m_\alpha$. For any $\alpha\in I$, let $g_\alpha \eqdef g|_{U_\alpha}$, $E_{\alpha} \eqdef E|_{U_\alpha}$, $\pi_\alpha \eqdef \pi|_{U_\alpha}$. Let $E^0_{\alpha}\eqdef U_\alpha\times \cM$ and $\pi^0_{\alpha}\colon E_{\alpha}^{0}\rightarrow U_\alpha$, $p^0_{\alpha}\colon E^0_{\alpha}\rightarrow \cM$ be the projections on the first and second factors. Then $\pi^0_{\alpha}\colon E^0_{\alpha}\eqdef U_\alpha\times \cM\rightarrow U_\alpha$ is the trivial fiber bundle over $U_\alpha$ with fiber $\cM$. Define diffeomorphisms $q_\alpha:E_{\alpha}\rightarrow U_\alpha\times \cM$ through: \ben q_\alpha(e)=(\pi(e), {\hat q}_\alpha(e))\, , \quad \forall\, e\in E_\alpha\, , \een where ${\hat q}_\alpha\colon E_\alpha\rightarrow \cM$ is given by the following differentiable surjective map: \ben \hat{q}_\alpha(e)\eqdef p^0_{\alpha}\circ (T_{\lambda^{\alpha}}\circ T_{\gamma^{\alpha}_{\pi(e)}})(e)=p^0_{\alpha}\circ T_{\lambda^{\alpha}\circ \gamma^{\alpha}_{\pi(e)}}(e)\in \cM\, , \qquad \forall\, e\in E_\alpha\, . \een Here we have used the identification $\cM\eqdef E_{m_{0}}$ and the fact that: \begin{equation*} (T_{\lambda^{\alpha}}\circ T_{\gamma^{\alpha}_{\pi(e)}})(e) \in \left\{m_{0}\right\}\times E_{m_{0}}\, , \qquad \forall\, e\in E_{\alpha}\, . \end{equation*} The restriction ${\hat q}_{\alpha}(m)\eqdef {\hat q}_\alpha|_{E_m}:E_m\rightarrow \cM$ to the fiber at $m\in U_\alpha$ is an isometry from $(E_m,h_m)$ to $(\cM,\cG)$ which is given explicitly by: \begin{equation*} {\hat q}_{\alpha}(m)(e_{m})=p^{0}_{\alpha}\circ T_{\lambda^{\alpha}\circ \gamma^{\alpha}_{m}}(m\times e_{m})\, , \quad \forall\, e_{m}\in E_m\, . \end{equation*} The maps $q_\alpha$ are diffeomorphisms from $E_\alpha$ to $E^0_{\alpha}=U_\alpha\times\cM$ which fit into the following commutative diagram: \ben \scalebox{1.2}{ \xymatrix{ E_\alpha ~~\ar[d]_{\pi_\alpha} \ar[r]^{\!\!\!\!\!\!q_\alpha} & ~~E^0_{\alpha} \ar[d]^{\pi^0_{\alpha}}\\ U_\alpha \ar[r]^{\id_{U_\alpha}} & U_\alpha \\ }} \een Hence $(U_\alpha, q_\alpha)$ is a trivializing atlas for the fiber bundle $\pi$, called the {\em special trivializing atlas} determined by the convex cover $(U_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$, by the reference point $m_0$ and by the choices of points $m_{\alpha}\in U_\alpha$ and of paths $\lambda^{\alpha}$ from $m_{\alpha}$ to $m_0$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.statement_short: Trivializing maps built from Ehresmann transport along geodesics inside each convex-cover element towards a reference point $m_0$.
nodes.genus: a trivializing atlas $(U_\alpha, q_\alpha)$ for the fiber bundle $\pi$
differentia: determined by the convex cover $(U_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$, by the reference point $m_0$ and by the choices of points $m_{\alpha}\in U_\alpha$ and of paths $\lambda^{\alpha}$ from $m_{\alpha}$ to $m_0$

nodes.name: $q_\alpha$ is an isomorphism onto a topologically trivial Kaluza-Klein space
nodes.statement: Let $h_{\alpha}\eqdef h|_{E_{\alpha}}$. Since the Ehresmann transport $T$ is isometric, the vertical metric $h_\alpha|_{V}$ agrees with $\cG^{p^0_{\alpha}}$ through the diffeomorphism $q_\alpha\colon E_{\alpha}\rightarrow U_\alpha\times \cM$. Hence $h_\alpha$ corresponds through $q_\alpha$ to a Kaluza-Klein metric $h^{0}_{\alpha}$ on the trivial bundle $\pi^0_{\alpha}:E_{\alpha}\rightarrow U_\alpha$. The latter is the Kaluza-Klein metric determined by $g|_{U_\alpha}$, $\cG$ and the distribution $H^{0}_{\alpha} \eqdef (\dd q_\alpha)(H_\alpha)$, where $H_\alpha\eqdef H|_{E_\alpha}$. The diffeomorphism $q_\alpha$ is an isometry from $(E_\alpha,h_\alpha)$ to $(E^0_{\alpha}, h^{0}_{\alpha})$ which makes diagram \eqref{ltriv} into an isomorphism of Kaluza-Klein spaces from the Kaluza-Klein space $\pi_\alpha:(E_\alpha,h_\alpha)\rightarrow (U_\alpha,g_\alpha)$ to the Kaluza-Klein space $\pi^0_{\alpha}\colon (E^0_{\alpha},h^{0}_{\alpha})\rightarrow (U_\alpha,g_\alpha)$. Notice that the second of these need not be a product Kaluza-Klein space, since $h^{0}_{\alpha}$ may differ from the product metric $g_\alpha\times \cG$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.statement_short: Each $q_\alpha$ is an isometry $(E_\alpha,h_\alpha)\to(E^0_\alpha,h^0_\alpha)$, though $h^0_\alpha$ need not be the product metric.

nodes.name: Every Kaluza-Klein space is locally topologically trivial
nodes.statement: Since $(M,g)$ admits convex covers, any Kaluza-Klein space admits special trivializing atlases. In particular, any Kaluza-Klein space is locally isomorphic with a topologically trivial Kaluza-Klein space (which need not be a product Kaluza-Klein space!).
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.statement_short: Convex covers exist, hence special trivializing atlases exist and every Kaluza-Klein space is locally topologically trivial.
assumptions: Since $(M,g)$ admits convex covers
conclusions: any Kaluza-Klein space admits special trivializing atlases
any Kaluza-Klein space is locally isomorphic with a topologically trivial Kaluza-Klein space (which need not be a product Kaluza-Klein space!)

nodes.name: transition functions $\bg_{\alpha\beta}$ of a special trivializing atlas
nodes.statement: For any $\alpha,\beta\in I$ such that $U_{\alpha\beta}\eqdef U_\alpha\cap U_\beta\neq \emptyset$, we have: \be (q_\beta\circ q_\alpha^{-1})(m,p)=(m, \bg_{\alpha\beta}(m)(p))\, , \quad \forall\, m\in U_{\alpha\beta}\, , \quad \forall\, p\in \cM\, , \ee where the transition functions $\bg_{\alpha\beta}:U_{\alpha\beta}\rightarrow \Iso(\cM,\cG)$ are given by: \ben \bg_{\alpha\beta}(m)\eqdef {\hat q}_\beta(m)\circ {\hat q}^{-1}_\alpha(m)\in \Iso(\cM,\cG)\, , \quad \forall\, m\in U_{\alpha\beta}\, . \een Using \eqref{hatqalpha}, this gives: \be \bg_{\alpha\beta}(m)=T_{\lambda^{\beta}}\circ T_{\gamma^{\beta}_{m}}\circ T_{\gamma^{\alpha}_{m}}^{-1}\circ T_{\lambda^{\alpha}}^{-1}= T_{c^{\alpha\beta}_m}\in \Iso(\cM,\cG)\, , \quad \forall\, m\in U_{\alpha\beta}\, . \ee
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.statement_short: The transition functions are the fiberwise isometries $\bg_{\alpha\beta}(m)=\hat q_\beta(m)\circ\hat q_\alpha^{-1}(m)=T_{c^{\alpha\beta}_m}$.

nodes.name: The closed path $c^{\alpha\beta}_m$
nodes.statement: Here: \ben c^{\alpha\beta}_m\eqdef \lambda^{\beta}\circ\gamma^{\beta}_{m}\circ (\gamma^{\alpha}_{m})^{-1}\circ (\lambda^{\alpha})^{-1}\, , \een is the closed path starting and ending at $m_0$ and passing through the point $m\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ which is shown in Figure \ref{fig:specialtriv}.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.statement_short: Transition functions are the transports along closed paths based at $m_0$ passing through $m$.

nodes.name: Local form of the vertical potential and $\bg_{\alpha\beta}\in\Iso(\cM,\cG,\Phi)$
nodes.statement: Let $\bPhi$ be a vertical potential for $\pi$. In this case, a special trivializing atlas for the Kaluza-Klein space $\pi$ is also called a special trivializing atlas for the scalar bundle $(\pi,\bPhi)$. Let $\bPhi_{\alpha} \eqdef \bPhi|_{E_\alpha}$ and set $\Phi\eqdef \Phi_{m_0}$. Since $\bPhi$ is $T$-invariant, the definition \eqref{hatqalpha} of ${\hat q}_\alpha$ implies: \ben \bPhi_\alpha=\Phi\circ {\hat q}_\alpha\, . \een This gives $\Phi\circ \bg_{\alpha\beta}=\Phi$, i.e. $\bg_{\alpha\beta}\in \Iso(\cM,\cG,\Phi)$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.statement_short: $T$-invariance gives $\bPhi_\alpha=\Phi\circ\hat q_\alpha$, hence the transition functions preserve $\Phi$.

nodes.name: Integrability makes the transition functions locally constant
nodes.statement: When the Kaluza-Klein space $\pi$ is integrable, the Ehresmann transport depends only on the homotopy class of curves in $M$. In this case, $T_{c^{\alpha\beta}_m}$ is independent of the point $m\in U_\alpha\cap U_\beta$ since $U_\alpha\cap U_\beta$ is path connected and hence the homotopy class of $c^{\alpha\beta}_m$ does not depend on $m$. Moreover, integrability of $H$ implies that $H_{\alpha}^{0}$ coincide with the trivial Ehresmann connections $H_{\alpha}^{\triv}$ of $\pi^0_{\alpha}$. In this case, $\pi^0_{\alpha}\colon (E^0_{\alpha}, h_\alpha)\rightarrow (U_\alpha,g_\alpha)$ is a product Kaluza-Klein space and $q_\alpha$ is an isometry from $(E_{\alpha}, h_\alpha)$ to $(U_\alpha\times\cM,g_\alpha\times \cG)$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.statement_short: For integrable $\pi$ the transport depends only on homotopy class, so $T_{c^{\alpha\beta}_m}$ is $m$-independent and $H^0_\alpha=H^{\triv}_\alpha$.
assumptions: When the Kaluza-Klein space $\pi$ is integrable
conclusions: $T_{c^{\alpha\beta}_m}$ is independent of the point $m\in U_\alpha\cap U_\beta$
$H_{\alpha}^{0}$ coincide with the trivial Ehresmann connections $H_{\alpha}^{\triv}$ of $\pi^0_{\alpha}$
$q_\alpha$ is an isometry from $(E_{\alpha}, h_\alpha)$ to $(U_\alpha\times\cM,g_\alpha\times \cG)$

nodes.name: Special trivializing atlases of an integrable Kaluza-Klein space
nodes.statement: Let $\pi:(E,h)\rightarrow (M,g)$ be an integrable Kaluza-Klein space. Then the local trivializing maps $q_\alpha$ of a special trivializing atlas consist on isometries from $(E_{\alpha}, h_\alpha)$ to $(U_\alpha\times \cM,g_\alpha\times\cG)$ and the transition functions $\bg_{\alpha\beta}$ defined by such an atlas are constant on $U_\alpha\cap U_\beta$. In particular, $\pi$ is locally isomorphic with a product Kaluza-Klein space.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.statement_short: For an integrable Kaluza-Klein space the local trivializations are isometries onto products and the transition functions are constant.
assumptions: Let $\pi:(E,h)\rightarrow (M,g)$ be an integrable Kaluza-Klein space
conclusions: the local trivializing maps $q_\alpha$ of a special trivializing atlas consist on isometries from $(E_{\alpha}, h_\alpha)$ to $(U_\alpha\times \cM,g_\alpha\times\cG)$
the transition functions $\bg_{\alpha\beta}$ defined by such an atlas are constant on $U_\alpha\cap U_\beta$
$\pi$ is locally isomorphic with a product Kaluza-Klein space

nodes.name: Cocycle relation for ${\hat q}_\alpha$ in the integrable case
nodes.statement: In this case, relation \eqref{bgdef} gives: \ben {\hat q}_\beta|_{E_{\alpha\beta}}=\bg_{\alpha\beta}\circ {\hat q}_\alpha|_{E_{\alpha\beta}}~~\forall \alpha,\beta\in I~~, \een where $E_{\alpha\beta}\eqdef E|_{\pi^{-1}(U_{\alpha\beta})}$ and we define $\bg_{\alpha\beta}\eqdef \id_\cM$ when $U_{\alpha\beta}=\emptyset$.
nodes.section: 2.4 Special trivializing atlases for a Kaluza-Klein space and for a scalar bundle
nodes.statement_short: ${\hat q}_\beta=\bg_{\alpha\beta}\circ{\hat q}_\alpha$ on overlaps, with $\bg_{\alpha\beta}=\id_\cM$ when the overlap is empty.

nodes.name: Constant transition functions preserve the potential
nodes.statement: Suppose that the integrable Kaluza-Klein space $\pi$ is endowed with a vertical potential $\bPhi$ whose restriction to $\cM$ we denote by $\Phi$. Then the constant transition functions in a special trivializing atlas satisfy $\bg_{\alpha\beta}\in \Iso(\cM,\cG,\Phi)$.
